claim: CD10neg neutrophils significantly correlated with levels of IL-1ß.

claim: CD101neg neutrophils isolated from ischemic myocardium 3 hr after reperfusion display increased expression of MMP-9.

claim: CD101neg neutrophils expressed IL-1ß at higher levels compared to CD101pos cells 24 hr after reperfusion.

claim: CD101neg neutrophils isolated from ischemic myocardium 24 hr after reperfusion have an immature morphology.

claim: Immature CD101neg neutrophils migrate and home to ischemic myocardium shortly after reperfusion.

claim: CD101neg neutrophils isolated from the ischemic region 24 hr after reperfusion were more resistant to apoptosis than their CD101pos counterparts.

source: These findings provide evidence that immature CD101neg neutrophils are able to traffic into lymph nodes after AMI, where they could contribute to regulation of lymphocyte effector functions.

claim: Persistent CMV infection is associated with higher IFN-γ levels in patients with increased frequency of CD10neg neutrophils.

claim: There is a relation among expansion of immature CD10neg neutrophils, CMV seropositivity and strongly enhanced levels of IFN-γ in patients with large AMI.
source: Not surprisingly, when stratified according to CMV serostatus, maximum levels of circulating IFN-γ among ACS patients were detected in CMV-seropositive STEMI patients displaying increased levels of CD10neg neutrophils (Figure 8E), indicating a relation among expansion of immature CD10neg neutrophils, CMV seropositivity and strongly enhanced levels of IFN-γ in patients with large AMI.

claim: CD10neg neutrophils strongly enhanced IL-12 production by CD4+ T-cells from CMV+ patients when co-cultured using a transwell system.
source: We found that CD10neg neutrophils strongly enhanced IFN-γ and IL-12 production by CD4+ T-cells from CMV+ patients (Figure 9A and B), when co-cultured using a transwell system where CD4+ T-cells in the lower chamber were separated from neutrophils in the upper chamber.
evidence: This is a finding from transwell co-culture experiments presented in Figure 9A and B.

claim: IL-12 production was significantly higher in CD4+ T-cells from CMV+ than CMV- patients.

claim: The addition of neutralizing anti-IL-12 antibody abrogated the IFN-γ production by CD4+ T-cells from CMV+ patients in presence of supernatants derived from CD10neg neutrophils.
source: The addition of neutralizing anti-IL-12 antibody abrogated the IFN-γ production by CD4+ T-cells from CMV+ patients in presence of supernatants derived from CD10neg neutrophils (Figure 9A).

claim: CD10neg neutrophils release soluble factors that efficiently induce a strong Th1 type response.
source: Our data indicate that CD10neg neutrophils release soluble factors that efficiently induce a strong Th1 type response.

claim: CD10neg neutrophils from CMV- and CMV+ patients exhibit the same ability to induce IFN-γ production by CD4+ T-cells.

claim: CD10neg neutrophils had no effect on CD3/CD28‐stimulated CD4+CD28null T-cells.
source: CD10neg neutrophils had no effect on CD3/CD28‐stimulated CD4+CD28null T-cells (Figure 9A and B), demonstrating that overproduction of IFN-γ is confined to CD4+ T-cells expressing CD28.

claim: Overproduction of IFN-γ in response to CD10neg neutrophils is confined to CD4+ T-cells expressing CD28.
source: CD10neg neutrophils had no effect on CD3/CD28‐stimulated CD4+CD28null T-cells (Figure 9A and B), demonstrating that overproduction of IFN-γ is confined to CD4+ T-cells expressing CD28.

source: Taken together, our findings indicate that CD4+CD28+ T-cells from CMV+ patients with AMI display a distinct phenotype overproducing IFN-γ in presence of immature neutrophils via induction of interleukin-12.
